title: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin
summary: Ipamorelin and tesamorelin are compared because both raise growth hormone, but only one is a medicine. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a stabilised GHRH analogue approved in the United States in 2010 to reduce abdominal fat in people with HIV-associated lipodystrophy, with phase 3 trials behind that single indication. Ipamorelin is a ghrelin-receptor agonist that was never approved and has two human trials. No study compares them directly. Tesamorelin's approved dose, 2 milligrams daily by subcutaneous injection, is the only regulator-reviewed dose of any compound in this comparison, and it applies to one narrow population.

seo.description: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin: an FDA-approved GHRH analogue with phase 3 trials against a ghrelin mimetic with two, the only approved dose, and no comparison.

faq.question: Is tesamorelin FDA approved?
faq.answer: Yes, since 2010, as Egrifta, for reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Other uses are off-label.

faq.question: Is ipamorelin FDA approved?
faq.answer: No. It has never been approved for any use.

faq.question: Which is more effective for fat loss?
faq.answer: Tesamorelin has phase 3 trials showing reduced visceral fat in people with HIV lipodystrophy; ipamorelin has no efficacy trial. In people without HIV, tesamorelin's effect is off-label and modest in the trials that exist; no comparison has been run.

faq.question: What is the approved tesamorelin dose?
faq.answer: 2 milligrams by subcutaneous injection once daily, for its approved indication. No dose of ipamorelin has been approved or established.

faq.question: Can they be combined?
faq.answer: Communities do, on GHRH-plus-ghrelin logic. No study has tested the pair.

faq.question: Are both prohibited in sport?
faq.answer: Yes, both under WADA S2, at all times.

open_questions: No study compares the two for any outcome.
Tesamorelin's effect outside HIV-associated lipodystrophy is off-label and modestly evidenced.
Ipamorelin has no efficacy trial in any population.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin in two minutes
guide.html:
One is a medicine. Tesamorelin is FDA-approved, since 2010, for one use: reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV who have lipodystrophy. It has phase 3 trials, a label, a defined dose of 2 milligrams daily, and a documented side-effect profile. Ipamorelin has none of those.

Different receptors. Tesamorelin is a GHRH analogue with substitutions that protect it from breakdown; ipamorelin acts on the ghrelin receptor. Both release growth hormone from the pituitary.

The catch. Tesamorelin's evidence is in a specific population for a specific outcome. Its use for general fat loss or body composition in people without HIV is off-label and, in trials that exist, modest. Ipamorelin has no efficacy trial at all.

Head to head. Nothing. No indexed study compares them.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin: the human trials side by side
guide.lede: One has a phase 3 programme. The other has two studies, one of them a failed trial.
guide.html:
Tesamorelin. In a 2011 trial, 273 people with HIV and excess belly fat took tesamorelin 2 mg daily and 137 took placebo for 26 weeks.{{cite:pmid-21516030}} In a 2014 randomized trial, deep belly fat fell by 34 cm² on tesamorelin and rose by 8 cm² on placebo over 6 months.{{cite:pmid-25038357}} In people with HIV and fatty liver, it reduced liver fat by 4.1 percentage points more than placebo, a 37% relative fall.{{cite:pmid-31611038}} Outside HIV, a 2012 trial in adults with obesity and low growth hormone also reduced deep belly fat against placebo{{cite:pmid-23015655}}, while a 2017 trial in type 2 diabetes found no change in insulin response or blood sugar control.{{cite:pmid-28617838}}

Ipamorelin. A 1999 study in healthy men showed it releases growth hormone at every dose tested, with a half-life of about 2 hours.{{cite:pmid-10496658}} Its one treatment trial, in 114 patients after bowel surgery, found no significant difference from placebo.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} It has never been tested for fat loss in people.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin side effects
guide.lede: Tesamorelin's side effects are documented because it went through trials; ipamorelin's are largely unknown for the same reason in reverse.
guide.html:
Tesamorelin. In a 2019 trial, the tesamorelin group had more injection-site complaints than the placebo group, none judged serious.{{cite:pmid-31611038}} Over 52 weeks it was reported as generally well tolerated.{{cite:pmid-18690162}} A 2024 analysis found side effects, including high blood sugar, no more frequent than on placebo{{cite:pmid-38905488}}. In a 2025 review of drug side-effect reports, carpal tunnel syndrome was reported more often than expected with tesamorelin, though such reports cannot show the drug caused it.{{cite:pmid-40510111}}

Ipamorelin. Its 2014 trial tracked side effects and laboratory tests, but the abstract reports no results.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} No other human safety data is on record.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin dosage in the studies
guide.lede: Doses studies administered, reported as published.
guide.html: Tesamorelin's trials in HIV used 2 mg under the skin once daily{{cite:pmid-25038357}}, which is also the approved dose for its one licensed use. A trial in 152 older adults used 1 mg a day, injected 30 minutes before bed, for 20 weeks.{{cite:pmid-22869065}} Ipamorelin's only treatment trial gave 0.03 mg/kg by infusion into a vein twice daily in hospital after surgery.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} No ipamorelin dose has been tested for the uses it circulates for. The tesamorelin schedule is on its dosing protocol.

guide.heading: Ipamorelin vs tesamorelin cycle length: how long studies gave each one
guide.lede: Treatment periods on record, not recommended courses.
guide.html: Tesamorelin trials ran for 26 weeks{{cite:pmid-21516030}}, 6 months{{cite:pmid-25038357}}, and in the fatty-liver trial 12 months followed by 6 months in which everyone took it.{{cite:pmid-31611038}} The 2008 long-term study followed people for 52 weeks.{{cite:pmid-18690162}} Ipamorelin's longest human course is up to 7 days of twice-daily infusions after surgery.{{cite:pmid-25331030}} Every compound's study durations are on the peptide cycle length page.

guide.heading: Who should avoid ipamorelin or tesamorelin?
guide.lede: Tesamorelin's trials name who they kept out. Ipamorelin's record names no one.
guide.html:
Tesamorelin. A 2017 trial excluded people with signs of breast or prostate cancer, recent steroid use, recent use of any growth hormone or IGF-1 product, pituitary disease, past head radiation, and current or past cancer.{{cite:pmid-28617838}} The trial in HIV-associated fatty liver also excluded heavy drinkers, people with hepatitis B or C or cirrhosis, and people with poorly controlled diabetes.{{cite:pmid-32701508}}

Ipamorelin. No exclusion criteria are on record, so there is no evidence-based list. That is an absence of evidence, not a sign that it suits everyone.

Both are named under section S2 of the WADA Prohibited List, prohibited at all times. The full lists are on the tesamorelin and ipamorelin pages.

guide.heading: How the two are discussed as choices
guide.html: The comparison usually arises for fat loss, and here the asymmetry matters. Tesamorelin has trials showing reduced visceral fat in a population with a specific metabolic condition, with a label that lists what went wrong in those trials. Ipamorelin has a reputation, from animal and volunteer pharmacology, and no outcome trial. A reader choosing between them is choosing between an approved drug used off-label and an unapproved compound used on faith; the label is also the reason tesamorelin's cautions, on glucose, IGF-1 and active malignancy, are known rather than theoretical. The two are also combined, as the tesamorelin and ipamorelin stack, on the same GHRH-plus-ghrelin logic as other blends; no study has tested that pair.
